messages:
todd: heads up — gnode-18 iops jumped ~3x around 02:13 UTC, scrub/trim cycle overlapped with batch reclaim. GPU provisioning started failing for preemptible pool.

kira: looking, any specific errors in janitor or kernel logs?

todd: logs show heavy fsyncs from scrubper and nvme controller resets. provisioning queue shows 'attach timeout' and 'evict stall'.

todd: paste logs:
```
kernel: nvme0: ctrlr reset, status 0x400
janitor: scrubper[4212]: fsync() 0x7ff... took 2.1s
provisioner: attach timeout gnode-18: gpu-alloc 0->queued
```

engbot: @channel Auto-alert: nvme_io_surge gnode-18 (severity: high) — initiating metric collection

prashant: can we temporarily lower scrub concurrency for eu-west2 pool? that's usually the quick win.

kira: +1. I decreased SCRUB_CONCURRENCY from 16 -> 4 on scratchpool-az1. Will monitor.

todd: changed cache eviction policy to aggressive LRU for affected nodes (patched via rollout id 7822). Will that help for new allocations?

sre-oncall: patch looks good. In flights: 12 preemptible gpu launches stuck — manually unblocked 6 by forcing ephemeral reattach.

todd: reattachments show `writeback backlog` still high on some disks; suspect write-amplification after overlayfs change last deploy.

kira: rollback overlayfs v2? we have a canary in eu-west2 that passed but this touches busy hosts.

prashant: before rollback, try a targeted fstrim + drop_caches on the worst hosts (gnode-18,19,21). low-risk and quick.

todd: running fstrim now on gnode-18 (sudo fstrim -v /scratch) — ETA ~30s.

engbot: @todd fstrim completed in 28s; reclaimed 1.2G on /scratch

todd: metrics improving: iops back to ~1.1x baseline, attach queue draining.

sre-oncall: leaving a follow-up task: create a throttle window for janitor between 01:30-03:30 UTC during heavy GPU batch deploys. Filing infra ticket.

kira: also add a probe to fail early if scrub concurrency + GPU queue depth > threshold (avoid cascade).

prashant: cost note — reducing scrub concurrency increases background GC time; will track impact on ephemeral disk life but preferable to blocking customer workloads.

todd: agreed. I'll add a small dashboard tile showing scrub concurrency vs gpu attach latency.

infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-1257: 'janitor-throttle-window + scrub-concurrency safety net' — CC: @eng-infra

sre-oncall: thanks, keep eyes on eu-west2 for next 24h. if we see repeat spikes, plan: stagger scrubs per-az and add ephemeral cache warming.

kira: ack. I'll follow up with numbers in the morning.

todd: thanks all :thumbsup:
